title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Maya Gonzalez
description:
Motivation: Reduce unit economics (cost per inference) by shipping automated defaults and tooling that pick batching, caching, and quantization profiles based on observed workload characteristics. This PR wires together three pieces: 1) runtime default heuristics for batching and prefix/KV caching that are conservative by default but can be autotuned; 2) a set of quantization profiles and an onboarding job that recommends a profile per model/workload; 3) unit-econ backend and Console UI surfaces to show estimated cost-savings and suggested rollout policies.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add AutoTune defaults service (controller + scheduler) that samples live traffic metrics and computes new suggested defaults for per-route batching_window_ms, max_batch_size, and cache_ttl. Suggestions are emitted as reviews that can be auto-applied with a rollout policy.
- Introduce quantization profiles (q4_0,q4_1,q8_0) metadata and a non-blocking offline evaluation job that estimates quality vs cost tradeoffs and surfaces a recommended profile.
- Unit economics tooling: backend endpoints to compute estimated tokens-per-second, cost-per-token, and projected monthly savings; Console changes to show per-route recommended profile, expected delta, and a quick-apply canary flow.
- Add telemetry hooks and E2E tests for the autotune flow and quantization evaluation pipeline.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime: default heuristics and safe fallback implemented
- [x] Autotune controller + scheduler implemented and feature-flagged
- [x] Quant profiles plus offline evaluator and evaluator integration tests
- [x] Unit-econ backend API + Console UI integration (beta)
- [x] Perf/regression tests + load test results attached
- [x] Docs: developer and user-facing docs updated

Notes on behavior and safety: suggestions are initially gated behind the feature flag `autotune-safe-rollouts`. The controller will never increase max_batch_size beyond the route's SLA envelope and will always keep a fallback to previous config to support instant rollback. Quantization recommendations are advisory by default; applying a profile requires an explicit rollout.

Performance summary: on internal A/B tests against high-throughput chat workloads we saw median cost-per-token reductions of 18%-28% depending on model and sequence length (q4_1 + batching + KV caching). Latency regression was <5th percentile for 95% of requests due to conservative batching window heuristics. Full load test logs are linked in the PR conversation.

Migration and rollout: ship behind feature flag, enable for internal customers, and run a 2-week canary on Dedicated pools before enabling for hosted traffic.

Related: ENG-4512 (autotune controller), ENG-4520 (quant evaluator), PM-321 (unit econ metrics and Console UX).
